summary: Iteration 16: landing/download page + public downloads endpoint + desktop helper app-window. Backend: 11/11 new pytest pass (live /api/public/downloads unavailable shape w/o auth; mocked GitHub release parsing -> available/1.0.7/3 links; partial assets; fetch failure -> unavailable; 10-min cache incl. expiry refetch; blank HELPER_REPO). Desktop core: import OK (VERSION 1.0.5), launch_options headless toggle, open_app_window Chrome --app=<server_url|https://shddw.com>/?app=1 with own --user-data-dir, webbrowser.open fallback. iter15 regression 10/10 pass. UI: signed-out / shows landing (all testids, 3 steps, Win+Mac install steps, open-app -> /sign-in, unavailable button 'Download coming soon' + web link, no version); nav Download anchors to #download; /download renders landing signed-in and out; /?app=1 signed-out -> /sign-in; signed-in / -> workspace; signed-in /?app=1 -> workspace. Stubbed endpoint: Windows UA -> 'Download Shadow for Windows' + mac_arm/mac_intel others; Mac UA w/o userAgentData -> 'Mac (Apple silicon)' + windows/mac_intel others; version line shown. Mobile 390px no horizontal overflow. No page errors.

minor.issue: Failed GitHub lookups are cached for the full 10 minutes (failure dict is truthy), so a transient GitHub error/rate-limit hides downloads for 10 min. Consider a shorter TTL (e.g. 60s) for failures.

ui_bugs.issue: When OS isn't detected, primary button falls back to first link ('Download Shadow for Windows') AND the same Windows link is repeated under 'Also for:' (others filter only excludes os=null). Exclude the fallback key from others or show a neutral 'Download Shadow' with all options.

integration_issues.issue: IN_APP is computed once from window.location at module load. After Clerk sign-in the app window lands on '/' without ?app=1; any later full reload + sign-out in the app window shows the marketing landing (with Download button) inside the installed app instead of /sign-in. Consider persisting app mode (sessionStorage) once ?app=1 is seen.

issues: Header still shows 'Sign in' and bottom CTA 'Open Shadow on the web' -> /sign-in; for signed-in users these should read 'Open Shadow' and link to '/'.

action_items: (Low) Use a shorter cache TTL for failed GitHub release lookups
(Low) Don't duplicate fallback link in 'Also for' when OS is unknown; consider neutral label
(Low) Persist app mode (?app=1) in sessionStorage so signed-out state inside desktop app window always goes to /sign-in
(Low) On /download for signed-in users, show 'Open Shadow' linking to '/' instead of 'Sign in'
critical_code_review_comments: detectOs relies on userAgentData.architecture === 'x86' to pick mac_intel; Safari/Firefox on Intel Macs have no userAgentData and will get the Apple-silicon dmg by default. The 'Also for' Intel link mitigates this; acceptable but worth noting.
main.py toggle_show calls helper.restart_browser() immediately, which would kill an in-progress task's Chrome; consider deferring restart until idle or warning the user.

open_app_window runs on every helper start (open_app_on_start True) even before pairing -> opens https://shddw.com/?app=1 (fine for production, but in preview it ignores the preview URL until paired).
seed_data_creation: None. HELPER_REPO not modified (only monkeypatched in-process during unit tests).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_iter16_downloads_landing.py (pytest.ini adds xdist; don't pass -p no:xdist). UI download-available states were tested by stubbing **/api/public/downloads via page.route in a new browser context with custom UA; headless Chromium on Linux reports userAgentData architecture 'x86', so Mac UA alone yields mac_intel — override navigator.userAgentData to test Apple-silicon path.
